goal: Run a Q1/Q2 2024 operational efficiency review for Meridian's four plants and check the VP memo's figures against the data. Deliver a five-tab diagnostic workbook (Plant Scorecard, Trend Diagnostics, Industry Benchmark vs FRED MCUMFN and defect-dataset percentiles, Complaint-Production Crossref, Equipment Risk Matrix), Meridian_COPQ_Analysis.csv with a summary row, and a 2-3 page strategic memo to David Chen that answers the board's consolidation question.
delivered: Three files in output/: Meridian_Operational_Efficiency_Diagnostics.xlsx (all five tabs, FRED Jan-Jun values averaging 75.835%, percentile positioning, plant/product watch items), Meridian_COPQ_Analysis.csv (per-plant and TOTAL rows, COPQ $428,935 = 3.51%) and Meridian_Strategic_Investment_Memo.docx (recommends targeted investment over consolidation; a 'Memo claims checked' paragraph covers Phoenix 58%, Portland 87.3% and headcount 820).
what_went_wrong: The core numbers were mostly right; the losses come from missing analyses and interpretations the rubric expects. No complaint-category breakdown was ever made (Dimensional Tolerance 15, Late Delivery 13, Portland 9 of 13), so R8 failed fully and R2 partly. Workforce and Phoenix framing were weak: the memo used a headcount-weighted turnover of 20.7% instead of the 23.2% departmental average, omitted the 2.4-year tenure and Phoenix's ~$81 cost per unit, and never said high turnover wastes training. The subagent had returned the exact figures (23.18%, 2.42 y, 43.88 h) plus the 'Columbus +18% YoY cannot verify' finding, but the root agent left them out. Trend Diagnostics shows only slopes, with no Portland monthly OTD series and no systemic-issue flag; the agent also switched from unweighted (92.7 to 86.4) to volume-weighted (93.0 to 85.6) OTD.

failed_items.why: FRED average (75.835%) and all four plant comparisons are correct, but the interpretation only says all plants exceed FRED; it never frames Phoenix (rank 4, 91.5%) as underperforming internal targets rather than the industry.

Complaint rates were correct (Portland 0.509 highest), but the Crossref has no category analysis (Dimensional Tolerance/Late Delivery) and no Portland severity split; the subagent had reported 'Portland 20 (5/6/6/3)' but it was not carried into the sheet.

Trend Diagnostics gives only Portland's OTD slope (-1.44 pp/month) and month-level WATCH rows, with no monthly OTD progression, no explicit flag of the downward slope, no VP-memo/92% SLA tie-in and no 'systemic' characterisation. At steps 37-41 the agent also switched to volume-weighted OTD (93.0 to 85.6), away from the simple averages (92.7 to 86.4).

The memo recommends against consolidation and cites Phoenix's lowest OEE and additive capability, but omits Phoenix's highest cost per unit (~$81), uses 20.7% weighted turnover with no tenure or 'ramp-up not structural' framing, and does not say Columbus's $2.66M capex is needed regardless of consolidation.

The subagent's message to root says 'Columbus +18% YoY downtime cannot verify (no 2023)' and lists other unverifiable claims, but the memo's 'Memo claims checked' covers only Phoenix 58%, Portland 87.3% and headcount, with no verifiable vs unverifiable distinction.

The memo reports headcount-weighted Phoenix turnover of 20.7% (not the 23.2% departmental average), no 2.4-year tenure and no 18/171 part-time split, and attributes training not translating into quality to missing certification rather than turnover. The subagent had supplied 23.18% and 2.42 y (L component).

No output file contains a complaint-category Pareto or a systemic vs plant-specific category split, although Complaint_Category is in the staged CSV. The prompt's Crossref spec did not ask for categories, and the agent never attempted this analysis.

The CSV has a TOTAL row summing units (161,387), rework (3,236) and every cost column the task specified (COPQ $428,935, 3.51%). It failed only for lacking a total-defects (~6,160) column, which the task's COPQ specification never asks for.

subagent_notes: One subagent inspected all inputs and sent the root detailed metrics: severity counts per plant (Portland 5 Critical/6 High), Phoenix tenure 2.42 y, turnover 23.18% and training 43.88 h, and that the Columbus +18% YoY claim cannot be verified. These matched the rubric, but the root left most of them out of the deliverables. Its volume-weighted OTD suggestion also led the root to replace the unweighted monthly OTD figures the rubric expects. Net effect: useful information whose value was lost at hand-off.
